findings.title: Eastern withdrawal as an oriented threshold
findings.claim: The sideward withdrawal into an eastern place forms an oriented threshold toward light before the wider disclosure associated with Maryam's story.
findings.mechanism: The focus occurrence of the withdrawal word supplies sideward movement and edge-position facets; the eastern adjective supplies light and directional facets, while the trusted cross-run record and the supplied Maryam, Spirit, refuge, and sign connections make their contact a threshold reading rather than a bare location label.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the place as a deliberately oriented edge from which an emergence is approached, while the plain movement from her family to a place remains intact.
findings.containment: This is an interpretive threshold and protection image, not a literal sanctuary, a claim about Maryam's motive, a sunrise-time assertion, or a replacement for the ordinary geographic place.

epistemic.reason: The trusted support anchors both focus branches and the focus supplies the cross-root contact; the light branch is lexically qualified and the threshold/protection result remains an interpretation.

findings.title: The remembrance command recurs as a narrative frame
findings.claim: The command to mention Maryam in the Book functions as one instance of a recurring narrative frame for presenting named figures.
findings.mechanism: The focus's spoken-mention carrier meets exact repetitions of the command-plus-Book frame at 19:41, 19:51, 19:54, and 19:56, so the local imperative operates as a repeated compositional act of bringing a named person into view.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see Maryam's mention as a deliberate textual presentation within a recurring frame, not merely as an isolated instruction to remember.
findings.containment: The recurrence is a compositional relation, not a surah thesis or a ranking of Maryam with the other named figures; it leaves the ordinary command and Book reading intact, and no target-side morphology is inferred.

epistemic.reason: The connection records supply exact target Arabic and explicit repeated-frame notes, while their qualification withholds target morphology and makes the compositional conclusion interpretive.

findings.title: Withdrawal crosses a formed family boundary
findings.claim: The phrase naming Maryam's family carries a close-bond community sense, and the supplied Maryam connections place that source group within a consecrated and guarded setting that the withdrawal crosses.
findings.mechanism: The possessive family occurrence supplies the focus carrier; the dedication, naming and protection, guardianship, and sanctuary connections return to Maryam's lineage and care setting, changing the family from a generic group into a formed relational boundary around the movement.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the withdrawal as a movement out of an already established bond of family, dedication, and guardianship, not simply a change of geographical location.
findings.containment: This does not identify every member of the family, assign a motive to the withdrawal, claim permanent severance, or use sanctuary as the literal meaning of the family word; target-side morphology is not inferred.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus carrier and target Arabic are supplied, and the connection notes explicitly identify dedication, protection, guardianship, and sanctuary; the wider relational synthesis remains qualified because target morphology is absent.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the place as the bounded scene where an extraordinary emergence comes into view, alongside its ordinary locative sense.
findings.containment: The focus word still means a place; this does not make it mean create, claim that the place causes conception, or import target-side morphology that the connection records do not supply.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch and carrier are exact, but the creative relation is a multi-step connection-based inference and the target records explicitly lack target morphology and lexical analysis.
